issues.label: Compliance with R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b)
issues.why: The court must determine whether the trial court complied with the statutory mandate to consider youth and its attendant characteristics before imposing an adult sentence.

issues.label: Whether error was forfeited/preserved
issues.why: Must assess whether Arrington objected below and how forfeiture affects review under Crim.R. 52.

issues.label: Plain error review standard
issues.why: If unpreserved, the court must decide whether the sentencing omission constitutes plain error under Crim.R. 52(B).

issues.label: Appellate review standard under R.C. 2953.08(G)
issues.why: The court must apply the felony sentence review standard governing whether the sentence is contrary to law.

issues.label: Effect of guilty plea on appeal rights
issues.why: Must consider whether the guilty plea waived or limited any sentencing challenges.

issues.label: Applicability of State v. Patrick
issues.why: The court must determine whether Patrick's requirement to consider youth in indefinite sentences governs this case.

issues.label: Immediate sentencing without presentence investigation
issues.why: The court proceeded straight to sentencing, raising whether adequate youth-related information was before it.

issues.label: Reagan Tokes indefinite sentence validity
issues.why: The 7-to-10.5-year indefinite term implicates the constitutionality and proper application of the indefinite sentencing scheme.

issues.label: Whether record shows youth consideration
issues.why: Court must review whether the sentencing record reflects any consideration of mitigating youth factors despite counsel's silence.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance: deficient performance
issues.why: Must evaluate whether counsel's failure to present youth mitigation fell below an objective standard of reasonableness.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance: prejudice
issues.why: Must determine whether a reasonable probability exists the sentence would differ had mitigation been presented.

issues.label: Availability of mitigation evidence in record
issues.why: The psychological evaluation and history existed, bearing on whether counsel unreasonably failed to use them.

issues.label: Ohio Const. Art. I, § 9 proportionality
issues.why: Arrington invokes the state constitutional provision regarding cruel and unusual/proportional punishment for juveniles.

issues.label: Validity of bindover/transfer proceedings
issues.why: The court may need to confirm the juvenile transfer was proper as a jurisdictional predicate to the adult conviction.

issues.label: Remedy if error found
issues.why: Court must decide whether to remand for resentencing or another remedy.

issues.label: Consideration of R.C. 2929.11 and 2929.12
issues.why: General felony sentencing purposes and factors may bear on whether the sentence is contrary to law.
